title: Framebuffer Draw Refresh Pipeline
description: A six-stage stepped pipeline tracing a drawing call from user code into the RAM framebuffer and out over SPI to the physical OLED, making the show() commit point visible.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Embedded Systems
Displays

learningObjectives: Explain why framebuffer changes are invisible until show() is called
Trace a text-rendering call through to lit pixels
Describe why multiple draws can share a single refresh
prerequisites: RAM holds data while a program runs
A display is a separate device connected by wires

controls.label: Step
controls.purpose: Advance one pipeline stage, wrapping after the last

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Return to the opening state and clear the glass

controls.label: Draw another line WITHOUT calling show()
controls.purpose: Add a shape to the framebuffer only

assumptions: The pixel grids are coarse mockups, not a true 128 x 64 rendering
SPI transfer is shown as a single atomic burst
limitations: Does not model partial-window updates, page addressing, or SSD1306 command framing

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through with a deliberately misconception-revealing default state
keyQuestions: Why does the framebuffer show Hi while the glass is blank?
At exactly which stage do the physical pixels change?
commonMisconceptions: That a drawing call updates the display immediately
That each drawing call causes its own screen refresh
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the screen contents after a sequence of draws with no show() call
